maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not think any
new apparatus was installed last year. This vote is for service, not for new construction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE

speechtext: Mines and geological survey-for administration of the Explosives Act (chap. 62, r.s., 1927), $10,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are there any salaries
in this item?

speakeroldname: Hon. W. A. GORDON (Minister of Mines):
speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is partly salary.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Then perhaps this item
could stand.
Item stands.
Miscellaneous-grant to Imperial Institute, $9,733.33.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Would the minister explain the reason for this grant?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: This is under an agreement with the United Kingdom and the other dominions. It is one of those institutions that were set up in Great Britain for the purpose of assembling information in connection with the mineral resources of the empire. Under the agreement each dominion contributes so much money, Canada's contribution being as is indicated in the item, S9,733.33.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is that in Canadian funds
or English currency?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I do not know.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
How long has this
agreement been in force between the government of this country and those of England and the other dominions?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: If I recollect aright, since 1923.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: How long has it to run?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
At the present time a
conference is taking place in London with a view to consolidating the various efforts such as this that have to do with assembling empire information with respect to many matters
Htfr. Duranleau.]
including minerals, and I am hopeful that after- this conference has concluded its work, all these matters will be consolidated in one information bureau. If that takes place, then this vote will disappear and probably be absorbed in a general vote covering items of this character.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Are any reports from
this Imperial Institute available at present?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: They have been available for eight years.

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I imagine there are reports, although I have seen them only when I have sought some special information. At times I have received information from the institute with respect to certain minerals. I have not seen any comprehensive annual report; I am not sure there is one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not wish to be
disrespectful, but as a matter of fact is the institute anything more than a post office, if I may so say, or a collection office through which are transmitted reports received from various parts of the empire? In other words, is a synopsis made of these reports and a new report published, or are just such pamphlets as are thought to be of use to some particular part of the empire transmitted through that office?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I would not go so far as
to say that it is merely a post office. It is essential, and the mining industry considers it essential, that information should be assembled from various parts of the empire showing what minerals they have in abundance, what minerals they are short of, what minerals we could export to them, what minerals we are short of and could get within the empire, and whether those mineral deposits have been developed or are capable of being turned into industry. Matters of that kind are assembled in the Imperial Institute and from time to time the Dominion of Canada has turned toward the institute for that information. Personally I believe the institute has been of more service to the colonies than to the dominions; that has been my view for some years, and I am not at all wedded to the continuance for any great period of time of this institute without a revision of its activities. As I said a few minutes ago, I believe after the conference to which I have referred these various activities will be coordinated, their expense reduced and their usefulness to those seeking information about various parts of the empire and their products increased.

Supply-M ines

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: What I was really trying to find out was whether anything was done there in the way of expert work or whether it was more or less clerical, if I may so term it, synopsizing the various reports received. It occurred to me that the transmission of these reports from various parts of the empire could, in these times when conditions are difficult, be done directly between the different parts of the empire instead of the information having to go through a central office, and that such reports as were useful to us could be used in our Department of Mines and others discarded rather than that they should all go to a central bureau and be distributed from it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Did I understand the minister to say that this institute had been in operation only since 1923?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is my recollection.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have an idea, unless I have the wrong name in my head, that this had been running for about forty years and that at one time it was considered as being of great advantage, but for some years it has died out altogether. Could this information not be obtained through Canada House?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I believe so.

Item agreed to.
Miscellaneous-to provide for payments in connection with the movements of coal under conditions prescribed by the governor in council and for the cost of administration thereof, $2,000,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Will the minister explain the increase of $250,000?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The increase is because
more coal has been moved subject to what is known as subvention. This increase is to take care of that extra movement of coal upon which subvention is paid.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Is this a rebate given to the
railway companies for transporting coal?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No. Under the coal subventions the money is paid to the producer of the coal, not to the railways. The subvention applies not only to a comparatively
small movement for the railways, but east and west for coal used for industrial purposes. That is where most of the money involved in this vote goes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does this cover payment to the coal mines in Vancouver island?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: As this amount is larger than formerly and as I presume we are voting it for the future, am I justified in assuming that the grants will be continued after they lapse as they will in June of this year?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is the intention of the
government at present to see that the various orders in council establishing the subventions are renewed, and those who contemplate making the usual spring contracts have been advised that it is the intention of the government to renew these subventions in order that there will be no anxiety in regard to entering into contracts for the coming year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: For what period will they be renewed-a year?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The subventions being payable out of a vote of this character are of necessity only for the current year, because they come out of money voted by parliament for the purpose and not under a statute. Therefore this will be until the end of the fiscal year 1934.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
But the existing grant runs
out in June, 1933. Will the government renew it for another year or will it be renewed only for nine months?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister of Labour; Minister of Mines
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: If it were possible to renew it for a whole year, I see no objection to doing so, but my view at the moment is that we can renew it only until the end of the next fiscal year. If it is renewed again, then it would be for a twelve months period.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-INSPECTION OF CANNED SALMON STATEMENT OF MR. NEILL ON MOTION OF MR. GUTHRIE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Or done by a supplementary estimate.
Progress reported.
At eleven o'clock the house adjourned, without question put, pursuant to standing order.
